sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Logan County?
sections.html:
The Logan County recorder works from the courthouse annex at 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine, OH 43311. The recorder's page gives 937-599-7201 as the phone number and lists the office as open Monday through Friday from 8:00 until 4:30. Wednesday is the day the office issues Veteran ID cards.

Ohio's recorder keeps the permanent record of who owns land and what liens or encumbrances sit on it. The office says it enforces more than 1,000 sections of the Revised Code, keeps land records in archival form and indexes each document so a searcher can build a chain of title. The same page notes that records pass through to title examiners, attorneys, genealogists and historians.

The Logan Online portal lists a Recorder's Document Search for looking up filed documents. The recorder also publishes Document Standardization Guidelines, a historical page and a Veteran ID Card Program page.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Logan County?
sections.html:
The county's recordable documents page prints a short schedule. Each charge applies to documents recorded in the county, and the recorder pays the fees into the county general fund.

Logan County document filing fees
ItemFee
First 2 pages$39
Each additional page$8
Non-standardization fee$20
Marginal reference, each$4

Source: Logan County Recordable Documents.

Call 937-599-7201 for the total on a long document or a deed that covers several parcels.

sections.h2: What layout rules can trigger the $20 fee in Logan County?
sections.html:
The $20 non-standardization fee applies when a document does not follow Ohio Revised Code 317.114. Logan County's guidelines page says the rule governs documents prepared after June 30, 2009, and it lists the requirements:

  • Computer font of at least 10 point.
  • Paper no smaller than 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Black or blue ink only, and no highlighting.
  • One-inch margins on each side and at the bottom of the page.
  • A three-inch margin at the top of the first page, reserved for the recorder, auditor and engineer.
  • A one and a half inch margin at the top of each remaining page.

The rule does not reach court documents, taxing authority documents, plats, DD-214 discharge papers, state or federal documents, or papers signed before the effective date. A downloadable standards template is on the same page.

sections.h2: What does the Logan County auditor do before the recorder?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the county auditor, whose office is also at 100 S. Madriver Street, before it is recorded. The auditor's forms page lists the paperwork a seller or buyer may need:

  • Conveyance Form DTE 100 for an ordinary sale, and DTE 100M for a manufactured home.
  • Exempt Conveyance DTE 100EX, or 100MEX for a manufactured home.
  • Agriculture Conveyance DTE 102.
  • Homestead Conveyance DTE 101.
  • Owner Occupied Credit Application DTE 105C and the Homestead Exemption Application DTE 105A.
  • Destroyed Property Application DTE 26 for a building that no longer stands.

Logan County also posts a Survey and Conveyance Standards PDF for legal descriptions and an online Conveyance Fee Calculator. Under Ohio Revised Code 319.202 the seller pays the conveyance fee, and a transfer tax is collected there only if the commissioners have levied one under Chapter 322. Ask the auditor which applies.

sections.h2: How does a Logan County forfeited land sale reach the recorder?
sections.html:
When delinquent taxes lead to a foreclosure and a property fails to sell twice, it is forfeited to the State of Ohio and handed to the auditor for sale. The auditor's published auction rules describe a sale at the Logan County Courthouse Annex, 100 S. Madriver Street. Properties sell "As-Is" and "Buyer Beware," and the auditor gives no representation about possession, eviction or prior inspection.

The winning bidder receives an Auditor's Deed. The rules say the auditor records it with the county recorder and delivers it to the purchaser, and the buyer becomes the legal owner when the auditor delivers the deed to the recorder. That deed extinguishes earlier title except for taxes and assessments not yet due, federal tax liens, easements and covenants running with the land. The rules bar a delinquent taxpayer or a current owner of the parcel from buying.

A bidder must pay in full or leave a minimum deposit of $1,000 per parcel on the sale date, and the balance is due within 10 calendar days. Those 2021 rules also list a $0.50 per parcel transfer fee and a $0.50 per parcel envelope and postage fee, in addition to recording.

sections.h2: When do Logan County property taxes come due, and how often is value reset?
sections.html:
The treasurer's home page showed July 22, 2026 as the second-half due date and counted 38,426 parcels. The office sits at 100 S. Madriver Street, Suite D, and answers at (937) 599-7223 on weekdays between 8:00 AM and 4:30 PM. The county's FAQ also describes an automatic withdrawal program that deducts the bill from a bank account on the final due date.

The auditor's FAQ explains the valuation calendar: reappraisals every six years, with a review and adjustment in the third calendar year after each one. Tax value is 35 percent of appraised market value. The Ohio Department of Taxation's schedule puts Logan County in a 2028 update and a 2031 reappraisal. Formal complaints go to the Board of Revision, which accepts them from January 1 through March 31. The board consists of the county auditor, the treasurer and the president of the board of commissioners or their representatives, and an owner can present recent appraisals or sales of similar property at the hearing.

sections.h2: What do Census figures and county history say about Logan County?
sections.html:
Logan County is in west central Ohio. According to the recorder's historical page, it was formed in 1818 from the northern part of Champaign County and named for Benjamin Logan, and Hardin County was split from it in 1820, becoming administratively separate in 1833. Bellefontaine is the seat and only city, and Wikipedia places Campbell Hill, Ohio's highest natural point at 1,549 feet, northeast of the city.

The Census Bureau QuickFacts table gives these 2020 to 2024 figures:

  • Population: 46,302 in July 2025, up 0.3 percent from April 2020.
  • A typical owned home is worth $203,200, and 77.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.
  • Owners with a mortgage spend $1,326 a month at the median, against $601 for those without one.
  • Gross rent has a median of $845.
  • The 19,560 households report a median income of $71,551.
  • Housing units in July 2025: 24,071. Building permits issued in 2025: 120.

sections.h2: What is the recorder's role in Ohio, and what is Torrens land?
sections.html:
The recorder's page traces the office to the Northwest Territory of 1787, when each county got a recorder's office. After Ohio became a state in 1803, the first legislature had the common pleas judges appoint a recorder in each county. The job became elective in 1829, and since 1936 the term has run four years.

The same page explains Torrens registration. In counties where certain parcels are registered under the Torrens Act, the boundaries are certified as correct and a state insurance fund guarantees the title. The county recorder is responsible for those registered land records. A seller who owns an unusual rural tract should ask the Logan recorder whether any part of it was registered.

The auditor, the treasurer and the recorder all list 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine as their address, so a closing agent can take the transfer, the tax question and the recording to one building.

faqs.q: How much does a standard two-page deed cost to record in Logan County?
faqs.a: The county's schedule lists $39 for the first two pages. Each additional page is $8, and a document that fails the standardization rules adds $20.

faqs.q: What are the Logan County recorder's hours?
faqs.a: The office at 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine opens weekdays at 8:00 and closes at 4:30. Its phone number is 937-599-7201.

faqs.q: Which documents escape the Logan County standardization fee?
faqs.a: Court documents, taxing authority documents, plats, DD-214 discharge papers and state or federal documents are exempt. So is anything executed before the law took effect.

faqs.q: Does the Logan County recorder help fill out deed forms?
faqs.a: The recorder keeps and indexes records. Ask a title company or an attorney to prepare the deed, and call 937-599-7201 for filing questions.

faqs.q: When does a forfeited land buyer own the property in Logan County?
faqs.a: Under the auditor's rules, the buyer becomes the legal owner when the auditor delivers the Auditor's Deed to the county recorder. The auditor records the deed and sends it to the purchaser.
